before.stem: ww The supraduodenal region of the common bile duct:

lies in the free margin of the greater omentum. 7%
lies to the left of the hepatic artery proper. 9%

before.stem: ww Regarding the rectus abdominis muscle, which of the following statements is INCORRECT:
options: It originates from the pubic crest, pubic tubercle and pubic symphysis. 8%
It inserts onto the costal cartilages of ribs 5 - 7 and to the xiphoid process. 12%
Itis separated in the midline by the linea alba. 6%
The free lower border of its aponeurosis forms the inguinal ligament.
Itis intersected along it length by tendinous intersections. 7%
before.explanation: The rectus abdominis is a long muscle that extends the length of the anterior abdominal wall. It originates from the pubic crest, pubic tubercle and pubic symphysis and inserts onto the costal cartilages of ribs 5 7 and to the xiphoid process. It is a paired muscle, separated in the midline by the linea alba. It is intersected along its length by tendinous intersections. The inguinal ligament is formed by the free lower border of the external oblique aponeurosis. ; Vv

after.stem: Regarding the rectus abdominis muscle, which of the following statements is INCORRECT:
options: It originates from the pubic crest, pubic tubercle and pubic symphysis.
It inserts onto the costal cartilages of ribs 5 - 7 and to the xiphoid process.
It is separated in the midline by the linea alba.
The free lower border of its aponeurosis forms the inguinal ligament.
It is intersected along its length by tendinous intersections.
warnings: Source page and external anatomy reference reviewed; remains an unapproved OCR draft.
after.explanation: The inguinal ligament is formed by the free lower border of the external oblique aponeurosis, not the rectus abdominis aponeurosis.
after.learningNote: The inguinal ligament is formed by the free lower border of the external oblique aponeurosis, not the rectus abdominis aponeurosis.
after.highYieldNote: The inguinal ligament is formed by the free lower border of the external oblique aponeurosis, not the rectus abdominis aponeurosis.

memoryAid.coreFact: The inguinal ligament is formed by the free lower border of the external oblique aponeurosis, not the rectus abdominis aponeurosis.

evidence.externalFinding: NCBI identifies the inguinal ligament as a thickened inferior portion of the external oblique aponeurosis; this supports the source's incorrect statement.

before.stem: ww The uterus receives its blood supply primarily from which of the following blood vessels:
options: Uterine branches of the ovarian artery 6%

Uterine branches from the umbilical artery 1%
